seed.why:
🔴 THE ARM THAT SEPARATES 'THE SIBLING WON' FROM 'THE TURN ENDED'.

The seeded arm returned 0/5 again, and the rival CHANGED: with an ontology present glossary_adopt_standards is no longer called at all, and glossary_extract_entities_from_doc takes the turn on 5 of 5, raising a Tier-A card that SUSPENDS it. So the precondition explanation is dead — but the runner's own caveat is now the live one: 'the turn ended before glossary_propose_batch's turn came, not that the model rejected it'. The ledger already knows this ambiguity: 'a THIRD of carded turns cannot tell rejected from unreached'.

APPROVING THE CARD RESOLVES IT. The turn continues past the sibling instead of dying at it.
  propose_batch STILL not called -> the sibling genuinely CONSUMES the request, and the row's
      'the model picks the sibling' is confirmed against its strongest alternative.
  propose_batch NOW called       -> the row is not a sibling-wins row at all; it is a
      CARD-TERMINATION row, every 0/5 it ever recorded is an artefact of the turn ending,
      and it must be re-filed under a mechanism it does not currently name.
